note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart. Claims about the world, such as how many courts a park has and whether it is lit, come from Lehi City Parks and the City of Orem Parks and are cited. Claims about coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Utah County. Two cities of the county are on this page, both read on 7 September 2026, and nobody working on this has played on any court in either.

slots.coverage:
Two cities in Utah County are published here: Lehi, with six venues and sixteen courts, and Orem, with three venues and twenty-two courts. Nine parks and thirty-eight courts between them, every one run by a city parks department.

Lehi's counts come from one page, "Welcome to Lehi City Parks", where each park has an "Address:" line and an amenity sentence in which the City counts what it has: "2 pickleball courts", "6 pickleball courts", "1 pickleball court". Orem's come from one page per park with a "Location:" line and an amenity list.

Provo, American Fork, Pleasant Grove, Springville, Spanish Fork and the County's own parks have no verified file behind this page, so none appears here. Both Cities name more courts than publish: Lehi counts courts at eleven parks and six of them can be placed, and Orem's Cascade Park carries "Pickleball/Tennis Courts" and no number at all.
slots.distribution:
Thirty-eight verified courts sit in nine parks. Orem holds three of the nine venues and twenty-two of the courts; Lehi holds six venues and sixteen.

Hillcrest Park's twelve, at 650 E 1400 S in south-east Orem, is the largest set in the county, and the City divides it on purpose: "6 Pickleball courts can be reserved for private use" through its online link, and six are held for the public on its "Paddle Rotation System". Two venues have six: Sharon Park at 600 N 300 E in north-east Orem, and Holbrook Farms Park on Drexler Drive in north-west Lehi, the largest count Lehi states at any park. Bonneville Park in Orem has four, Olympic Park in west Lehi three, and Allred, Stagecoach Large, Watercress and Centennial have two, two, two and one.

Lighting splits the county once. Bonneville's "Four Lighted Pickleball Courts" are the only lit courts either City states, and the other thirty-four carry no lighting answer either way. No page in either city states a price or writes the word free, and neither City states indoor or outdoor, surface or hours for a court. Every Lehi venue shares the 84043 postcode; Orem's three sit in 84097 and 84057.
slots.gaps:
The largest gap is inside Lehi, and it is an address problem rather than a court problem. The City counts courts at eleven parks and prints an address for each, but five of those addresses resolve in neither the Census address file nor OpenStreetMap as written: "3050 W. Traverse Mountain Blvd" for Shadow Ridge Park, "3109 W. Allred Dr." for Salix Park, "1987 West 1450 South" for South Creek Park, "2108 S Bullrush Pkwy" for Spring Creek Park and "2333 W. Northridge Dr" for Northridge Park. Twelve stated courts wait behind the first four. Northridge would be refused in any case, because "a pickleball court" is an article and not a number. In Orem the gap is one park: Cascade carries "Pickleball/Tennis Courts" and no number, and its page answered 404 on the day it was read.

Neither City states a surface, a court's hours, or whether any court is indoor or outdoor. Lehi states no lighting for any court, and its "pavilion lighting" at Centennial lights a pavilion. Hillcrest's "Hours of Operations: Monday-Saturday from 10:00am-8:00pm" sits under the heading "Splash Pad Hours", so it is not read as court hours.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Utah County?
faqs.a: Nobody knows the whole number. What has been checked is 38 courts across nine parks in two cities, 22 in Orem and 16 in Lehi, each with a source and a date you can see. Lehi's own page states twelve more at four parks whose addresses do not resolve.

faqs.q: Which venues in Utah County have lights?
faqs.a: One that the operator states: Bonneville Park in Orem, whose amenity line reads "Four Lighted Pickleball Courts". Every other court in the county is recorded as lighting not verified.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Not stated anywhere. No Lehi or Orem page prints a price or the word free. Lehi's sentence that "All other amenities are open to the public" is about access rather than cost, and Orem's reservation rules say who may book a court, not what it costs.

faqs.q: Can I book a court anywhere in the county?
faqs.a: At Hillcrest Park in Orem, where "6 Pickleball courts can be reserved for private use" through the City's online link and the other six run on its paddle rotation. Sharon Park's courts are reserved "ONLY" for the City's tournaments. In Lehi, "Reservations are for pavilion use only", so no court can be booked.

sources.evidence: All three Orem addresses matched in the Census address file as written and were placed in Utah County, UT (FIPS 49049) inside "Orem city": "650 E 1400 S, OREM, UT, 84097", "600 N 300 E, OREM, UT, 84057", "1450 N 800 W, OREM, UT, 84057". Olympic Park and Centennial Park in Lehi matched the same way, "2700 W PARKSIDE DR, LEHI, UT, 84043" and "2250 N 600 W, LEHI, UT, 84043", inside "Lehi city". Four Lehi addresses resolved through OpenStreetMap at house-number level because the Census file holds no record of Holbrook Farms or Stagecoach Large, drops the "N." from Allred Park Rd., and answers 1500 N for Watercress's 1500 South. Shadow Ridge, Salix, South Creek, Spring Creek and Northridge resolved in neither. Snapshots: data/sources/lehi-county-census.json, data/sources/orem-county-census.json
